column1: # Security guards, and the edit that removes each one.
# Read by scripts/verify-guards.sh. Tab-separated, four fields:
#   file <TAB> search <TAB> replace <TAB> ctest-target:test-name
# The point is not the list. The point is that a guard here is proven to be
# LOAD-BEARING: remove it and the named test must go red. A test that stays
# green when its guard is gone is measuring something else, and there is no way
# to tell that apart from a passing test by looking at a passing test.
# This exists because that happened. Twice on 2026-08-23 a hand-applied
# neutralisation silently did not match the source -- once because the
# replacement text ignored an if-init-statement -- so nothing was neutralised,
# the test passed, and the guard was recorded as proven when nothing had been
# proven at all. The script refuses a search string that does not appear, which
# is the whole fix: a neutralisation that cannot be applied is a failure, not a
# pass.
# `search` must be a single line and must appear EXACTLY ONCE in the file.
# Not every guard in the codebase is here. These are the ones where being wrong
# means reading somebody else's mail, sending plaintext, or handing a message to
# the wrong account.
# --- the decrypted message must not outlive its account -----------------
app/mail/MailController.h

# Text.textFormat defaults to Text.AutoText, which hands anything tag-shaped
# to the rich-text parser -- and that parser fetches over the QML
# engine's own QNetworkAccessManager, outside WebEngine, where neither
# settings.autoLoadImages nor RemoteContentInterceptor can see it. A subject
# header beacons the moment the list lays out.

# build one and look at it.

# NOT LISTED, deliberately: the other forty textFormat lines in app/qml,
# including the one this section was written for -- the inbox timestamp at
# MobileRoot.qml, which rendered the relay's raw atUtc string. Neutralisation
# cannot reach them. QmlTests instantiates leaf components; the sites that
# matter live in MobileRoot's inbox delegate and EmailDetail's headers, which
# need every C++ singleton to load, and QML cannot read a file at runtime to
# check them statically (XMLHttpRequest refuses local and qrc URLs unless
# QML_XHR_ALLOW_FILE_READ is set).
# They are gated statically instead, by the textFormat check in
# tests/qml/qmllint-gate.sh (ctest QmlPropertyLint): a Text or Label that
# binds anything other than a literal without declaring a SAFE format fails
# it. Delete the textFormat at MobileRoot.qml's timestamp and that test goes
# red. This harness cannot say so -- it neutralises a line and runs a compiled
# test binary, and QmlPropertyLint is a shell script -- which is why it is
# written down here instead.
# "Safe" is checked by value, not by presence: Text.RichText and
# Text.StyledText feed the same parser as the AutoText default, so they are
# accepted only over a literal, a translation of literals, or a value that
# goes through escapeHtml() -- directly or via a function in the same file
# that does. That last clause is what makes AutocompleteDropdown's
# highlighted() legal. Proven by hand, since the harness cannot: replacing
# Format.escapeHtml(text) with String(text) in AutocompleteDropdown.qml:67
# turns QmlPropertyLint red on both of that file's RichText bindings.
# ALSO NOT LISTED, for the same harness reason: the copy-before-call in
# core/pgp/OpenPgpDecryptor.cpp's verify block. gpgme documents the
# gpgme_verify_result_t as living only until the next operation on that
# context, so `status` is read into a local before the key lookup runs.
# Neutralising that would leave every test green on gpgme 2.1.2, which does
# not actually clobber (gpgme_get_key runs on a private context of its own --
# measured: same address, fields intact). It is written the safe way because
# the contract, not that implementation detail, is what this file supports
# across gpgme 1.x and 2.x.
# --- a wipe that unlinks the live database opens a replacement -----------
# TrackedWipe::recoverIfInterrupted() is the one wipeEverything() caller that
# does NOT relaunch: it finishes an interrupted wipe at startup and falls
# through into a full session. Without the reopen that session keeps writing
# through a connection bound to the unlinked inode, where the write either
# fails outright or is invisible to the next launch -- which cursors.ini
# (erased by the wipe, then repopulated by the re-pair's sync) tells is
# already up to date.
core/domain/LocalDataWipe.cpp
# The mirror: the reopen must NOT fire for a session that was never on that
# file. Under Hostile Location Protection main() opens ":memory:" while
# LocalDataWipe still holds the on-disk path so a leftover file gets erased --
# reopening there would create the one thing the mode exists to prevent.
core/domain/LocalDataWipe.cpp
# The SQLCipher key goes only once the file it opens is confirmed gone.
# QFile::remove() genuinely fails -- a non-writable profile directory, an
# EPERM -- and clearing the key over a surviving encrypted database bricks the
# profile for good: the next launch mints a new key, finds nothing to migrate,
# fails the open, and hits main()'s qFatal ABOVE the tripwire recovery that
# would have finished the wipe.
core/domain/LocalDataWipe.cpp
# --- a KDF that could not RUN is not a wrong pin -------------------------
# AppLockManager counts wrong guesses toward a ten-attempt wipe that erases
# the mail cache, the pairing credential and the lock. Argon2id wants a 64 MiB
# working set, and a cgroup-capped or low-memory session refuses it
# deterministically -- so collapsing "could not derive" onto "wrong pin" means
# a user typing the CORRECT pin is wiped. The KDF this replaced (PBKDF2) had
# no allocation failure mode, so nothing upstream was watching for one.
